newsitem.title: THAILAND: Thailand reiterates curbs on offshore baht deals.
newsitem.headline: Thailand reiterates curbs on offshore baht deals.

text.p: The Bank of Thailand has again told commercial banks, finance and securities firms to stop foreign exchange transactions with foreign institutional clients that could contribute to speculation in the baht.

The central bank said in a circular to financial institutions on May 28, a copy of which was obtained by Reuters on Monday, that financial institutions should suspend all foreign exchange swap deals that give foreign partners access to baht funds including currency and interest rate swaps, forward rate agreements, currency and interest rates options.
The Bank of Thailand also told Thai-based institutions to stop selling baht to foreign clients through forward outright or straight forward baht/dollar agreements.

It also asked banks and finance firms to accept by paying only in dollars for all unmatured baht-denominated bills of exchange, promissory notes, certificates of deposit and other debt instruments, including debentures and bonds.
The central bank circular follows almost similar directives issued to local financial institutions after the latest speculative attack on the baht in mid-May.

The Bank of Thailand won its war with speculators by choking off baht supply from the domestic market to foreign speculators and making it very expensive for them to procure the Thai unit in other markets.

The central bank in mid-May asked banks to block normal baht supply for speculators by quoting punitive baht/dollar swap rates amounting to more than 1,000 percent per year in a bid to stop market attacks on the baht.
The move, creating two-tier offshore and onshore baht rates, was effective in halting speculative attacks on the baht.

Currency dealers said the central bank instructions were meant for plugging loopholes for foreign speculators to find baht funds to cover their earlier short-baht positions or to further bet against the Thai currency.
The central bank circular instructed Thai institutions to report details of their foreign exchange transactions on a daily basis.

It said the ban on providing baht supply to foreign institutional partners was only temporary and would not apply to transactions involving imports, exports, direct and equity portfolio investment. The central bank said institutions providing these unaffected transactions must retain documentary evidence or seek prior official approval of cases that may breach the ban.

The Bank of Thailand said the new measures are essential during the time that the baht came under speculative pressure but they should not disrupt normal capital flows arising from trade and investment.
